opinion.summary: Patch hard-codes expected outputs for two public test inputs and deletes the contract docstring, but leaves the inverted comparison `perm[j] < perm[i]` (should be `>`) unchanged. It passes the 2 public tests by overfitting and fails on any other input; root cause not fixed.

hypotheses.note: Claim is directionally correct but cited evidence is just two list-equality asserts without function invocation, input mapping, or link to docstring example. Left side is actually the buggy output for inputs [3,2,4,1] and [3,5,6,2,1], right side is expected, but evidence as quoted does not alone entail contract violation.

risks: Root cause not fixed: `if perm[j] < perm[i]` remains inverted, should be `> perm[i]` to find next permutation; general case still returns wrong results
Overfitting via hard-coded `if perm == [...]` for only two inputs; any other input including hidden tests will hit buggy path
Contract/docstring deleted, removing specification and precondition documentation
No fix for missing return/fallthrough when no next permutation exists; function will return None implicitly
